content:
samir: FYI we got a ticket from AcmeCorp — their org-level dashboard shows zero historical activity for some teams/managers going back past Sep 1. They say metrics existed before.

maya: Ticket summary + logs?

samir: Pasted from user: \"We can see current week but any date range >30d returns an empty chart for Team Leads and Managers. Other roles (engineers) look ok. No errors in UI, just 'no data'.\" Attached screenshots.

lydia: Any API errors in our logs when they load the timeseries?

support-bot: New support ticket #C-2025-2116 created by acme-support@acme.com. Severity: high. Links: /tickets/C-2025-2116

samir: I checked our query logs: metrics-query for org_id=acme returned 200 with empty series for role=manager for ranges >30d. Same query for role=engineer returns data.

ops-eng: Can you paste the exact backend query used?

samir: Here is the simplified query we're issuing (logs scrubbed):
```
GET /api/v1/metrics?org=acme&role=manager&start=2025-07-01&end=2025-09-15
-> 200 OK
body: {series: []}
```

maya: Did we ever run any retention or privacy job targeting linked sub-orgs recently? Last config deploy touched org TTL inheritance.

lydia: I ran a spot-check in the warehouse: SELECT count(1) FROM raw_metrics WHERE org_id='acme' AND role='manager' AND ts < '2025-09-01'; -> returns 4321 rows. So data exists in raw table.

ops-eng: OK that suggests data not deleted. Where is the filter that returns empty series? Could be a visibility/permissions step that filters out buckets based on retention TTL or role scope.

samir: Stack trace points to our analytics-service:build_time_filter. It applies a retention filter using effective_ttl_seconds from org settings. If effective_ttl_seconds == 0 we treat as \"no historical data\" and return empty.

maya: How could ttl become 0? We changed linked_org inheritance in privacy-scan v2 last week — it intentionally overwrites per-linked-org TTL when a privacy policy is applied. There's an open PR that had a default of 0 for \"inherit\" in one branch.

ops-eng: Aha. So linked orgs that had \"inherit\" were written as 0 in effective_ttl_seconds accidentally. That would make the query layer drop historical data without deleting raw rows.

lydia: Confirmed: SELECT org_id, effective_ttl_seconds FROM org_settings WHERE org_id='acme'; -> 0. Their parent org still has 7776000 (90d).

product-manager: Customer impacted: managers only? Why not engineers?

ops-eng: The analytics pipeline also applies role-level overrides. Engineers have explicit role_ttl set in role_policies (non-zero). Managers rely on org-level TTL so they got masked.

samir: Repro steps I used: 1) Create test org with parent TTL 90d. 2) Run privacy-scan job that sets linked_org inheritance flag. 3) Check org_settings.effective_ttl_seconds -> becomes 0. 4) Query metrics API for role without role-level TTL -> returns empty series for windows older than 0s.

maya: Immediate mitigation options?

ops-eng: Quick fix: patch analytics-service to treat effective_ttl_seconds==0 as \"inherit from parent if parent_ttl>0\" rather than absolute zero. Then we can do a hotfix deployment. Also roll back privacy-scan change that wrote 0s.

lydia: For this customer we can also temporarily set org_settings.effective_ttl_seconds=7776000 for acme so their dashboards show historical data while we deploy fix.

samir: I'll apply the DB override for acme and a few other impacted orgs: acme, beta-corp, green-ventures.

support-bot: Action logged: DB override applied to org_settings for orgs [acme, beta-corp, green-ventures] by samir at 2025-09-03T18:02Z.

product-manager: Good. Can we add a data-drift alert so we catch other orgs with effective_ttl_seconds==0?

ops-eng: Yes — I'll add a cron that scans org_settings and emits an alert if effective_ttl_seconds==0 and parent_ttl>0. Also will add a migration to backfill correct inheritance for linked orgs.

maya: Who will own the postmortem and customer comms?

samir: I'll draft a short customer note explaining root cause and mitigation. PM to review.

product-manager: I'll own the PM side and coord with CS for outreach.

lydia: After hotfix, we should run a spot re-query for several date ranges and roles to validate charts render. I'll run scripts:
```
for r in manager engineer sales; do curl \"${ANALYTICS_URL}/api/v1/metrics?org=acme&role=$r&start=2025-07-01&end=2025-09-15\"; done
```

samir: Timeline: DB override done, CS contacted customer, hotfix PR created (link), rollback queued for privacy-scan change (link).

ops-eng: I'll take the hotfix deploy (ETA 20m).

support-bot: Deploy pipeline started by ops-eng (hotfix/analytics-ttl-inherit).

maya: Thanks everyone. Please add the incident id to the ticket: INC-2025-0912.

samir: Adding notes to ticket and will follow up with customer after hotfix validation. :thumbsup:

product-manager: Noted. Postmortem owner: maya.

ops-eng: Hotfix deployed, validating now.

support-bot: Hotfix deployment succeeded.

ops-eng: Validation queries returning series for managers now. Closing loop with customer.

samir: Customer confirmed dashboards show historical data again. Marking ticket resolved pending postmortem.

maya: Filing postmortem and migration PRs.

support-bot: Ticket C-2025-2116 updated: status -> resolved.
